messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT PD-9453 - Auth proxy unusual outbound traffic detected. Large number of POSTs to external bucket from edge-proxy svc. Paging @sre-oncall and @security.
sarah: I’m on it. grabbing logs and checking recent deploys. can someone confirm which tenants use edge-proxy today? :eyes:
ops-bot: Quick snapshot of suspicious requests:
```
2026-03-17T09:02:13Z edge-proxy PUT https://s3.amazonaws.com/malicious-bucket/key.part  200 x-token:eyJha... (truncated)
2026-03-17T09:02:14Z edge-proxy PUT https://s3.amazonaws.com/malicious-bucket/idx.log  200 x-token:eyJhb...
```
mike_sre: copy. are tokens real session tokens or svc acct creds? dan_security - any intel from threat feed?
dan_security: early look -> tokens appear to be user session JWTs (short-lived) being replayed. pattern shows 'session-shadow' header present. could be leakage from a debug log forwarder. investigating indexer and logdrain configs.
aisha_eng: I’m running a quick grep across the last 6h for `PUT .*s3.amazonaws.com` and `edge-proxy` in logs now. ETA ~5m.
sarah: rollback? we had a small logging sidecar change rolled 2h ago to staging and 1h ago to canary. not yet in prod-wide.
mike_sre: don't rollback blindly. we need containment first: 1) block outbound host at egress-firewall for that bucket pattern, 2) rotate any exposed session/session-store keys, 3) freeze S3 bucket (contact cloud team) and preserve objects. I'll open network ACL now.
ops-bot: egress rule applied: blocked outbound to s3.amazonaws.com for edge-proxy fleet (canary). Added temporary WAF rule to drop requests with header `session-shadow`.
aisha_eng: grep results: found ~120 requests from 10 unique session ids in last 15m. they map to 6 customer accounts (IDs redacted). I’m extracting sample traces.
dan_security: sample trace shows `x-forwarded-for` from internal telemetry relay (10.200.5.12) then proxied. suggests logs were forwarded with raw headers. suspect log-forwarder misconfigured to include full headers -> leak.
lex_legal: Lex here. If customer data left the environment we need to notify impacted customers and start preservation. Also please collect exact list of accounts and timestamps. I’ll stand by for tenant list and legal notif cadence.
sarah: handoff: I’ll be oncall for next 30m then pass to @mike_sre. documenting actions in incident ticket.
mike_sre: taking over at 09:20. proposed mitigation plan:
- rotate service tokens for `edge-proxy` immediately (scripts/rotate_keys.sh edge-proxy)
- revoke active user sessions via auth service for affected tenants
- disable log-forwarder ingestion for dev/staging pipeline until audit
- snapshot and quarantine S3 artifacts
- run forensic export of last 24h logs
aisha_eng: running rotation script now (starting background job). output:
```
$ ./scripts/rotate_keys.sh edge-proxy
rotating key pair for svc edge-proxy... new key id: key-20260317-01
propagating to fleet... done
scheduling old key revoke in 5m
```
dan_security: good. also enabling additional alerting on unusual PUT rate per service and adding a rule to detect `session-shadow` header presence.
ops-bot: Created incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-5821. Added playbook checklist + owner tags.
lex_legal: please redact the sample artifacts before any external share. we will follow PII disclosure policy; I want an initial notice drafted if we confirm data exfil.
sarah: confirmed 6 impacted customers. minimal data tiers (request metadata + some headers). no large PII blobs in samples so far but continuing to audit. preparing tenant list for legal.
mike_sre: I'm revoking sessions for impacted tenant ids now (auth revoke job queued). will also trigger full service-account rotation for any long-lived creds associated with the forwarder.
aisha_eng: dev pipeline log-forwarder disabled. canary staging pipeline still offline. looking for misconfig in forwarder config: `include_headers: true` found in rolling config - likely the culprit.
dan_security: timeline so far:
- 08:50 deploy: logging sidecar config change (canary)
- 09:01 spike: first suspicious PUTs observed
- 09:03 PD alert fired
- 09:05 containment rules applied (egress block)
- 09:10 key rotation started
mike_sre: customer-facing comms draft: short notice saying we detected unauthorized outbound transfer of limited request logs from an internal forwarder tied to edge-proxy; we have blocked the transfer, rotated keys, and are investigating scope. Legal to review.
lex_legal: draft ack received, will loop in compliance and privacy. Flag: notify customers within 72 hours if confirmed. gather full artifact list in ticket.
sarah: passing oncall to @mike_sre now. I’ll remain in channel for context. :thumbsup:
mike_sre: taking lead. next steps: finalize tenant list, confirm artifacts quarantined, coordinate with cloud team to freeze external bucket, and schedule postmortem. tagging @security for deeper forensics.
ops-bot: Follow-up tasks created in INF-5821: egress-unblock-testing, forwarder-config-audit, forensic-export, customer-notice-draft.
dan_security: I’ll start a full host-level audit on the telemetry relay and check for other exfil sinks. sharing initial findings within the ticket in 45m.
mike_sre: setting severity to P1 and creating an incident bridge: https://zoom.redwood/incident/PD-9453. All hands invited who were paged.
lex_legal: note: preserve chain-of-custody. do not delete artifacts.
sarah: ack. closing immediate actions on my side — handing off. stay in channel for updates.
ops-bot: Incident PD-9453 status: containment in place, rotation started, tickets opened. Next update in 30m or on significant change.
